docs.title: About
docs.text:
smallcat-chonk

A small, modular data catalog.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install smallcat-chonk

Do not install it next to the original smallcat. Both distributions put the same importable package, smallcat, in site-packages, so they overwrite each other's files, and uninstalling one removes files of the other. Use one or the other in an environment.

docs.title: Define connections
docs.text:
Connections live in a file (or in Airflow), never inline in the catalog. Each one has a name that catalogs and models refer to; they are validated when loaded.

# connections.yaml
connections:
    local:
        conn_type: fs
        extra:
            base_path: /tmp/smallcat-example/
    lake:
        conn_type: google_cloud_platform
        extra:
            bucket: my-bucket

docs.title: Create Catalog
docs.text:
Local catalogs can be kept in YAML files.

entries:
    foo:
        file_format: csv
        connection: local
        location: foo.csv
        load_options:
            header: true
    bar:
        file_format: parquet
        connection: lake
        location: bar.parquet
        save_options:
            partition_by:
                - year
                - month

docs.title: Standalone
docs.text:
from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")
catalog = Catalog.from_yaml("catalog.yaml", connections=conns)
catalog.save_polars("foo", df)
df2 = catalog.load_polars("foo")

A connection name that is not in conns fails when the catalog is loaded, not on the first read.

docs.title: Filter on load
docs.text:
load_polars (and the lower-level Arrow loaders) accept optional where and columns arguments to push filters and projections down to DuckDB/Arrow when reading:

df = catalog.load_polars(
    "bar",
    where="event_date >= '2024-01-01'",
    columns=["event_date", "user_id"],
)

docs.title: Lazy scans
docs.text:
scan_polars returns a Polars LazyFrame: nothing is read until collect(), and the filters and columns you chain are pushed down to the storage layer. On S3/GCS this means only the needed columns and row groups are downloaded.

import polars as pl

df = (
    catalog.scan_polars("bar")
    .filter(pl.col("event_date") >= pl.date(2024, 1, 1))  # Polars expressions, not SQL
    .select("event_date", "user_id")
    .collect()
)
load_polars scan_polars Engine DuckDB Polars' own reader (Parquet) / delta-rs + Polars (Delta) Filter where="amount > 10" (SQL string) .filter(pl.col("amount") > 10) Reads Everything the query needs, immediately Nothing until collect() Real lazy scan n/a Parquet and Delta. CSV and Excel are loaded eagerly and wrapped, so nothing is skipped

Notes:

  • Parquet and Delta use the connection's credentials through the same options (aws_*, google_service_account*). For Parquet, the DuckDB-only load options binary_as_string and file_row_number raise a ValueError in scan_polars; use load_polars for those.
  • Existing limits apply: IAM role, SSO and AssumeRole credentials are unverified against real AWS, and GCS needs a service account for Delta/scan_polars but HMAC keys for DuckDB.
  • Requires polars>=1.31.0.

docs.title: With Airflow
docs.text:
from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog

conns = Connections.from_airflow(["lake"])      # resolved and validated now
catalog = Catalog.from_airflow_variable("example_catalog", connections=conns)
df = catalog.load_polars("bar")

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
A model describes a dataset: its columns, where it lives and how it is stored. Model.objects reads and writes it as Polars DataFrames, validated against the model. The model never names a connection: the registry does, per environment.

import polars as pl
from smallcat import Connections, Model, ModelFileFormat, ModelWriteMode, registry

class Customer(Model):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str | None = None

    class Meta:
        location = "silver/customers"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.PARQUET

registry.load_connections(Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml"))
registry.register(Customer, connection="lake")

Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 10).select("id", "name").all()  # DataFrame
Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 10).lazy()                      # LazyFrame
Customer.objects.save(df, mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE)               # mode is required
  • mode is required: OVERWRITE replaces the whole dataset, APPEND adds rows and MERGE inserts the rows with a new key and updates the ones whose key exists (both Delta only; MERGE never deletes). Declare the key in Meta.merge_keys = ["id"] or pass it with save(df, mode="merge", merge_keys=["id"]).
  • allowed_write_modes in Meta limits what a model may do ([] is read-only); registering can restrict it further per environment, never widen it.
  • validation_mode is STRICT (types must match) or COERCE (cast, failing only on values that cannot be cast without loss).

See Models and a runnable example and a walk-through of querying with filter, where, all and lazy.

docs.title: Catalog reference
docs.text: load_options and save_options are optional, file_format is required and unknown keys are rejected. See the catalog reference for every option, the validation rules and the credentials each format uses.

docs.title: Catalog reference
docs.text:
A catalog is a mapping of dataset names to entries. It can be written in YAML, stored in an Airflow Variable, or built from a Python dictionary.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NRGConsulting/smallcat/refs/heads/main/schemas/catalog.schema.json
entries:
  customers:
    file_format: csv
    connection: local_raw           # a name defined in Connections
    location: customers.csv

  sales:
    file_format: parquet
    connection: datalake_gcs        # a name defined in Connections
    location: sales/2025/
    load_options:
      hive_partitioning: true
    save_options:
      overwrite: true
      partition_by: [region]

  events:
    file_format: delta_table
    connection: datalake_gcs
    location: silver/events
    save_options:
      mode: append

docs.title: Entry fields
docs.text: Field Required Description file_format yes One of csv, excel, parquet, delta_table. connection yes The name of a connection loaded in Connections (or an Airflow connection id). An inline mapping still works but is deprecated. location yes Path of the dataset, relative to the connection's base. load_options no Options applied when reading. Omit it to use the defaults. save_options no Options applied when writing. Omit it to use the defaults.

docs.title: Options per format
docs.text:
Format load_options save_options csv columns, sep, header, sample_size, all_varchar header, sep, overwrite parquet binary_as_string, file_row_number, hive_partitioning, union_by_name overwrite, partition_by, write_partition_columns excel header, sheet, range, all_varchar, empty_as_varchar header, sheet delta_table version, without_files, log_buffer_size mode, partition_by, schema_mode, merge_keys, update_columns

Boolean options are always forwarded, so header: false really turns the header off.

docs.title: Delta: mode: merge
docs.text:
mode is append, overwrite, ignore or merge. With merge, rows are matched on merge_keys: the ones that match are updated and the new ones are inserted.

entries:
  customers:
    file_format: delta_table
    connection: datalake_gcs
    location: silver/customers
    save_options:
      mode: merge
      merge_keys: [id]
      update_columns: [name, email]   # optional; default: every column but the keys
  • merge_keys is required with merge and not allowed otherwise: with any other mode, or with no mode at all, the catalog is refused when it is loaded. The keys are never updated.
  • update_columns (optional) limits which columns are overwritten on matching rows; new rows are always inserted whole. It cannot include a key.
  • If the table does not exist, the first save_polars creates it.
  • The data must not contain null or repeated keys (it fails before writing) and its columns must already exist in the table. schema_mode is not supported with merge.
  • merge never deletes rows (#32 tracks deletion).
  • It is only available for delta_table; Databricks-hosted tables are not supported.
  • DeltaTableDataset.update(path, predicate, values) sets columns to constant values on the rows a predicate selects (it is not exposed on the catalog).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The catalog is validated strictly when it is loaded:

  • file_format is required in YAML and dictionaries. An entry without it is rejected instead of being read as CSV.
  • Unknown keys are rejected everywhere (catalog, entries and options), so a typo such as hedaer is reported instead of silently ignored.
  • load_options and save_options may be omitted.
entries:
  broken:
    file_format: csv
    connection: my_conn
    location: a.csv
    load_options:
      hedaer: true      # extra_forbidden: unknown option

Note

Entries built in Python (CSVEntry(connection=..., location=...)) keep file_format as a default, so it only has to be written explicitly in YAML and dictionaries.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
location is always joined under the connection's base, and leading slashes are ignored. The path is normalized (a/./b//c becomes a/b/c) and glob patterns such as data/**/*.parquet are kept as they are.

A location that would climb out of the base (../x, a/../../x) is rejected with a ValueError when the entry is used:

entries:
  leak:
    file_format: csv
    connection:
      conn_type: fs
      extra:
        base_path: /data/raw
    location: ../../etc/passwd    # escapes /data/raw

catalog.load_polars("leak")   # ValueError: Path escapes the base location

Without base_uri or base_path, an fs connection resolves paths relative to the current working directory.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
connection is the name of a connection. Define the connections in a Connections (YAML or Airflow), load them first and pass them to the catalog, which checks every name when it is loaded:

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")
catalog = Catalog.from_yaml("catalog.yaml", connections=conns)

Without connections=, a name is resolved through Airflow the first time it is used. The definition of a connection is the mapping described below, whether it lives in a Connections file or (deprecated) inline in an entry.

Inline connections are deprecated

A connection written as a mapping inside an entry still works but emits a DeprecationWarning, because it puts credentials in the catalog.

A connection definition is validated when it is loaded, against the schema selected by its conn_type:

  • conn_type is required and must be fs, google_cloud_platform (or its alias google) or aws (alias s3). Any other value is rejected.
  • Unknown keys are rejected, both at the top level and inside extra, so a typo such as base_pth is reported instead of ignored.

Supported top-level keys are conn_type, host, schema, login, password and extra.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
password, aws_session_token, keyfile and keyfile_dict are secret values. Once the catalog is loaded they are held as Pydantic SecretStr, so they do not appear in repr(), str(), logs, validation errors or model_dump():

entry = catalog.entries["raw"]
entry.connection.password                       # SecretStr('**********')
entry.connection.password.get_secret_value()    # the real value
  • entry.get_connection() returns the plain values (it is what the datasets receive, like an Airflow connection). Do not log its result.
  • keyfile_dict accepts a mapping or a JSON string; it is stored as JSON text.
  • A connection given by id is resolved by Airflow, which keeps its own protection of the password.
  • The secrets are not encrypted at rest: in a YAML file or an Airflow Variable they are plain text. Prefer an Airflow connection (or a secrets backend) over an inline connection for real credentials.

docs.title: Local filesystem (fs)
docs.text:
connection:
  conn_type: fs
  extra:
    base_path: /data/raw       # or base_uri: file:///data/raw

extra is optional; both keys are optional too (see Locations).

base_path and base_uri may be written as Windows paths (C:\data, C:/data or file://C:\data): they are normalized to file:///C:/data.

Creating a dataset (or a catalog) never touches the filesystem. The directory of a destination, including nested ones such as reports/2025/out.csv, is created when the data is saved. delta_table entries leave that to delta-rs.

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage (google_cloud_platform)
docs.text:
connection:
  conn_type: google_cloud_platform
  extra:
    bucket: my-bucket
    prefix: raw                # or base_uri: gs://my-bucket/raw

Credentials depend on the engine that reads the data, which is not only a matter of the format: load_* and scan_polars use different engines for Parquet.

Read with Formats Engine Credentials load_* csv, parquet, excel DuckDB HMAC keys: the connection's login (key id) and password (secret). load_* delta_table delta-rs Service account: keyfile_dict, keyfile or key_path in extra. scan_polars parquet Polars Service account (same keys as above). scan_polars delta_table delta-rs and Polars Service account (same keys as above). scan_polars csv, excel DuckDB (eager) HMAC keys: they are loaded with load_polars and wrapped.

google is accepted as an alias of google_cloud_platform by every format.

A connection can carry both kinds of credentials: each engine uses the one it understands, so the same connection serves load_* and scan_polars on the same Parquet file. A mismatch does not fail silently: a DuckDB-based read with only a service account, or a delta-rs or Polars read with only HMAC keys, emits a UserWarning and accesses the bucket without credentials.

Incoherent settings are rejected when the connection is validated (and again when a dataset uses an Airflow connection id):

  • login and password must come together.
  • Only one of keyfile_dict, keyfile and key_path may be set.

Note

DuckDB cannot authenticate with a service account, so load_* on CSV, Parquet and Excel needs HMAC keys. Delta and every scan_polars on Parquet need a service account. To use both ways of reading the same Parquet file, put both kinds of credentials in the connection (see Parquet on GCS: load and scan).

docs.title: Amazon S3 (aws)
docs.text:
connection:
  conn_type: aws
  extra:
    bucket: my-bucket
    prefix: raw                    # or base_uri: s3://my-bucket/raw
    region_name: eu-west-1

The extra names are the ones of the Airflow aws connection, so an Airflow connection id of that type can be used as well.

extra key Description bucket, prefix Build the base URI s3://bucket/prefix. base_uri Explicit base URI; takes precedence over bucket/prefix. region_name AWS region. endpoint_url Endpoint of an S3-compatible store such as MinIO (http://minio:9000). Uses path-style requests, and plain HTTP when the URL says http://. profile_name Profile of the AWS config files to take credentials from. aws_session_token Session token that goes with static keys.

Credentials. There are two mutually exclusive ways to authenticate:

  • IAM roles and the AWS credential chain (recommended): leave login and password empty. The credentials are found the way the AWS SDK finds them: environment variables, web identity (EKS service accounts), ECS task roles, EC2 instance profiles, SSO and the shared AWS files. To assume a role, define a profile with role_arn and source_profile in ~/.aws/config and name it in profile_name.
  • Static keys: login is the access key id and password the secret access key (plus aws_session_token for temporary keys).

Combining static keys with profile_name, or giving only one of login and password, is rejected.

Formats Engine How the credential chain is resolved csv, parquet, excel DuckDB By DuckDB's aws extension. parquet (scan_polars) Polars By Polars itself, with the same rules as delta-rs below. delta_table delta-rs By delta-rs itself (environment, web identity, ECS, instance profile). With profile_name, the credentials are resolved by DuckDB and handed to delta-rs; they are temporary and are not refreshed during a long operation.

Delta tables on S3 are written without DynamoDB locking, which relies on S3 conditional writes.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text: Databricks connections are rejected with NotImplementedError when reading or writing Delta tables. An inline mapping with another conn_type is rejected when the catalog is loaded.

docs.title: Filtering on load
docs.text: where must be a single boolean expression over the dataset's columns, for example amount > 10 AND name IN ('a', 'b'). It is parsed before it runs and a ValueError is raised for statements, comments left open, subqueries or anything that changes the shape of the query. columns accepts plain column names only. Examples of every way of reading, from the connection to the result, are in Querying a catalog.

docs.title: Extensions and network access
docs.text: Reading or writing local files needs no network access. The DuckDB httpfs extension is loaded only for remote storage (gs://, s3://, https://), and the excel extension (and the aws extension, for the credential chain of S3 connections) is installed on first use and then reused from DuckDB's cache.

docs.title: Airflow
docs.text: Airflow is optional and is only imported when needed, for instance to resolve a connection id or to call Catalog.from_airflow_variable. Importing smallcat does not import Airflow.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
Connections is the one place where connections are defined. You load it first, and then hand it to whatever needs connections: a Catalog or a model registry (see Models). Both refer to a connection by name.

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

# connections.yaml
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: /data
  warehouse:
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket

Each definition is the same mapping described in the catalog reference (fs, google_cloud_platform and aws, with the same keys and the same credentials).

docs.title: Where connections come from
docs.text:
Loader Source Name of each connection Connections.from_yaml(path) A YAML file with a connections mapping The key Connections.from_dict(dict) A dictionary with the same structure The key Connections.from_airflow_variable(id) An Airflow Variable holding that structure as JSON The key Connections.from_airflow([ids]) Airflow connections, resolved with BaseHook The Airflow connection id

There is no way to pass a connection inline to a catalog or a registry on purpose: everything comes from a file or from Airflow, so credentials stay out of application code.

# Airflow: the ids are resolved and checked right now
conns = Connections.from_airflow(["lake", "warehouse"])

docs.title: Validated when loaded
docs.text:
Every loader checks the connections as it loads them, so a mistake fails at start-up and not on the first read.

  • Definitions from YAML, a dictionary or a Variable are validated against the schema chosen by conn_type. Unknown keys are rejected, so base_pth is reported instead of ignored.
  • Airflow connections must exist, have a supported conn_type (fs, google_cloud_platform/google, aws/s3) and an extra that is valid JSON. Their other fields are not checked: Airflow connections usually carry keys that smallcat does not use.
  • All the problems are reported together:
ConnectionsValidationError: Invalid connections:
  - lake.extra.base_pth: Extra inputs are not permitted
  - warehouse: Input tag 'ftp' found using 'conn_type' does not match any of the expected tags: ...

Error messages name the connection and the field but never include the values, so a password cannot end up in a log. repr(conns) shows only names and types: Connections(lake:fs, warehouse:google_cloud_platform).

Error Raised when ConnectionsValidationError A definition is invalid (also a ValueError). ConnectionNotFoundError An Airflow connection id does not exist (also a LookupError). ConnectionNotLoadedError A name is used that was never loaded. The message lists the names that are. DuplicateConnectionError Two sets of connections define the same name.

docs.title: Using them
docs.text:
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog

catalog = Catalog.from_yaml("catalog.yaml", connections=conns)

# catalog.yaml
entries:
  sales:
    file_format: parquet
    connection: warehouse        # a name in `conns`
    location: sales/

The names are checked when the catalog is loaded. If sales pointed to a name that is not in conns, Catalog.from_yaml would raise ConnectionNotLoadedError listing every entry affected and the names that are available, before anything is read.

Without connections=, a name is still resolved through Airflow the first time it is used, as before, so existing catalogs keep working.

Inline connections are deprecated

A catalog entry whose connection is a mapping instead of a name still works, but emits a DeprecationWarning: it puts credentials in the catalog. Move the definition to a Connections and refer to it by name.
