def all(self, *, as_models: bool = False) -> "pl.DataFrame | list[M]":
    """Run the query and return a DataFrame, or model instances.

    Args:
        as_models: If true, return one instance of the model per row
            instead of a DataFrame. Each row is validated by Pydantic, so
            field constraints apply.

    Returns:
        The rows as a DataFrame with the model's columns in its order, or
        as a list of instances when `as_models` is true.

    Raises:
        ModelQueryError: If `as_models` is true and the query uses
            `select()`, since instances need every required field.
        ModelSchemaValidationError: If the data does not match the model.
    """
    if not as_models:
        return self._frame()
    if self.columns is not None:
        msg = "as_models() needs every field: remove select()"
        raise ModelQueryError(msg)
    rows = self._frame().iter_rows(named=True)
    return [self.model.model_validate(row) for row in rows]

def _frame(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Run the query and return the validated DataFrame."""
    ctx = _context(self.model)
    selected = list(self.columns) if self.columns else None
    if self.where_sql is not None:
        df = ctx.entry.load_polars(where=self.where_sql, columns=selected)
        return validate_frame(df, ctx.spec, ctx.mode, selected)

    plan, raw = self._plan(ctx)
    try:
        df = plan.collect()
    except (pl.exceptions.InvalidOperationError, pl.exceptions.ComputeError):
        if ctx.mode is ModelValidationMode.COERCE:
            # Find out which column and how many values, from the raw data.
            raw_df = (raw.select(selected) if selected else raw).collect()
            validate_frame(raw_df, ctx.spec, ctx.mode, selected)
        raise
    check_nulls(df, ctx.spec, selected)
    return df

def _plan(self, ctx: _Context) -> tuple[pl.LazyFrame, pl.LazyFrame]:
    """Build the lazy plan and return it with the unfiltered scan."""
    selected = list(self.columns) if self.columns else None
    raw = ctx.entry.scan_polars()
    prepared = prepare_lazy(raw, ctx.spec, ctx.mode, selected)
    frame = prepared.frame
    if self.filters:
        frame = frame.filter(*self.filters)
    return frame.select(prepared.select), raw

class ModelSchemaValidationError(ModelError, ValueError):
    """A DataFrame does not match the schema declared by a model.

    Attributes:
        model_name: Name of the model class.
        issues: Every mismatch found, so they can be fixed in one go.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_name: str, issues: list[SchemaIssue]) -> None:
        """Build the error from the list of mismatches."""
        self.model_name = model_name
        self.issues = issues
        lines = "\n".join(f"  - {i.column}: {i.problem}" for i in issues)
        super().__init__(f"{model_name} does not match its schema:\n{lines}")

docs.title: smallcat.models.lookups
docs.text:
Django-style lookups for where(): job_id__lte=2 and friends.

A lookup is written as <field> or <field>__<operator> and a value:

Customer.objects.where(job_id=42)
Customer.objects.where(job_id__lte=2, country="ES")
Customer.objects.where(status__in=["new", "open"], deleted_at__isnull=True)

Lookups are resolved when the query is built, against the fields of the model: an unknown field, an operator the field's type does not offer or a value of the wrong type raises :class:ModelQueryError right where you write it. Nothing is defined per model: the fields and their types are read from the model itself.

They are rendered to an SQL predicate (DuckDB). Names come from the model and values are typed literals that this module quotes, so nothing the caller passes is ever interpreted as SQL.

Operators:

  • exact: equal. It is the default when no operator is given. Takes one value, or None (the same as isnull=True).
  • ne: not equal. One value, or None.
  • lt, lte, gt, gte: less than, less than or equal, greater than, greater than or equal. One value.
  • in: equal to any of the values. A list, tuple or set; an empty one matches nothing.
  • range: between two values, both included. A pair (low, high).
  • isnull: True for is null, False for is not null. A bool.
  • contains, startswith, endswith: text matches. A str; % and _ in it mean themselves.

Which operators a field accepts depends on its type (see :data:OPERATORS).

def lookups_to_sql(schema: ModelSchema, lookups: Mapping[str, object]) -> str:
    """Render lookups as one SQL predicate, joined with AND.

    Args:
        schema: The schema of the model the lookups refer to.
        lookups: Lookup names and their values, e.g. ``{"job_id__lte": 2}``.

    Returns:
        The SQL predicate (DuckDB).

    Raises:
        ModelQueryError: If there are no lookups, a name is not a field of the
            model, an operator is not available for the field's type, or a
            value does not suit the field.
    """
    if not lookups:
        msg = "where() needs lookups such as job_id__lte=2, or sql='...'"
        raise ModelQueryError(msg)
    parts = []
    for key, value in lookups.items():
        spec, operator = _resolve(schema.model_name, schema.fields, key)
        parts.append(_condition(spec, operator, value, key))
    return " AND ".join(parts)

def kind_of(dtype: pl.DataType) -> str:
    """Return the kind of a field, which decides its operators and its values.

    Args:
        dtype: The canonical Polars type of the field.

    Returns:
        One of the keys of :data:`OPERATORS`.
    """
    if dtype.is_integer():
        return "int"
    if dtype.is_float():
        return "float"
    simple = {
        pl.String: "str",
        pl.Boolean: "bool",
        pl.Date: "date",
        pl.Time: "time",
    }
    for polars_type, kind in simple.items():
        if dtype == polars_type:
            return kind
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Datetime):
        return "datetime"
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Duration):
        return "duration"
    return "other"

docs.title: Catalog with Airflow
docs.text: Use smallcat-chonk with Airflow. In this example we'll work locally by reading connections and variables from the Local Filesystem Backend. In production we could deploy the same DAG but the variables and connections would be defined in the database or a Secret Backend

docs.title: Install smallcat-chonk
docs.text:
Airflow is an optional dependency of smallcat-chonk, available as the airflow extra.

pip install "smallcat-chonk[airflow]"

or

uv add "smallcat-chonk[airflow]"

docs.title: Point Airflow to local secrets files
docs.text:
Configure the Local Filesystem Secrets Backend:

AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKENDS=airflow.secrets.local_filesystem.LocalFilesystemBackend
AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARGS='{"connections_file_path":"/path/to/connections.yaml","variables_file_path":"/path/to/variables.yaml"}'

Replace the paths with real locations.

docs.title: Define a connection (local filesystem)
docs.text:
connections.yaml:

local_filesystem:
  conn_type: fs
  extra:
    base_path: /tmp

docs.title: Define a sample catalog variable
docs.text:
variables.yaml:

my_catalog:
  entries:
    # Raw daily weather data
    foo:
      file_format: csv
      connection: local_filesystem
      location: foo.csv
      save_options:
        header: true
      load_options:
        header: true

    # Transformed output we’ll write
    foo_processed:
      file_format: csv
      connection: local_filesystem
      location: foo_processed.csv
      save_options:
        header: true
      load_options:
        header: true

This declares two datasets under /tmp:

  • foo.csv (input)
  • foo_processed.csv (output).

docs.title: Example DAG
docs.text:
The example pulls the Seattle weather CSV, stores it as foo, then creates a filtered/augmented dataset foo_processed:

  • parse dates
  • keep 2012-01-01 to 2012-03-31
  • keep only rainy/drizzly days
  • add temp_range = temp_max - temp_min
from datetime import datetime
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.decorators import task
import polars as pl

from smallcat.catalog import Catalog


SOURCE_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vega/vega-datasets/master/data/seattle-weather.csv"

def transform(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """This would usually be a function that you import and you have tested in notebooks"""
    return (
        df
        .with_columns(pl.col("date").cast(pl.Date))
        .filter(
            pl.col("date").is_between(pl.date(2012, 1, 1), pl.date(2012, 3, 31))
            & pl.col("weather").is_in(["rain", "drizzle"])
        )
        .with_columns((pl.col("temp_max") - pl.col("temp_min")).alias("temp_range"))
        .select("date", "precipitation", "temp_max", "temp_min", "weather", "temp_range")
    )

with DAG(
    dag_id="example_smallcat_weather",
    start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    schedule="@once",
    catchup=False,
) as dag:
    @task
    def get_input_data():
        """We can use the catalog to save input data.
        Only used so we have some data to work with.
        This would usually be a Data Engineering process"""
        catalog = Catalog.from_airflow_variable("my_catalog")
        raw_df = pl.read_csv(SOURCE_URL)
        catalog.save_polars("foo", raw_df)

    @task
    def ds_pipeline():
        catalog = Catalog.from_airflow_variable("my_catalog")

        df = catalog.load_polars("foo", where="date >= '2012-01-01'")
        out = transform(df)     # Function should be pure, only IO happens in the pipeline with the catalog
        catalog.save_polars("foo_processed", out)

    get_input_data()
    ds_pipeline()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    dag.test()

After the run, check /tmp/foo_processed.csv for the transformed result.

docs.title: Fail early on a missing connection
docs.text:
In the DAG above, connection: local_filesystem is resolved through Airflow the first time the entry is used. To check every connection the catalog names when it is loaded, load them first:

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_airflow(["local_filesystem"])   # must exist and be valid
catalog = Catalog.from_airflow_variable("my_catalog", connections=conns)

See Connections.

docs.title: Connections with a catalog
docs.text: How a connection reaches a catalog, without any other dependency: define it once in a file, load it, hand it to the catalog, and name it in each entry. To do the same inside Airflow, see Airflow.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
pip install smallcat-chonk

or

uv add smallcat-chonk

The script below writes its files under a temporary directory, so you can run it as it is:

python connections_catalog.py

docs.title: 1. Define and load the connection
docs.text:
Connections live apart from the catalog and are referred to by name.

# connections.yaml
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: /data

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

For a bucket, only this definition changes: see Google Cloud Storage and Amazon S3.

docs.title: 2. Hand it to the catalog
docs.text:
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog

catalog = Catalog.from_yaml("catalog.yaml", connections=conns)

Each entry names the connection in connection:. The names are checked when the catalog is loaded:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NRGConsulting/smallcat/refs/heads/main/schemas/catalog.schema.json
entries:
  people:
    file_format: csv
    connection: lake           # a name in `conns`
    location: people.csv       # /data/people.csv
    load_options: {header: true}
    save_options: {header: true}

The # yaml-language-server line gives you validation and auto-complete for the catalog in VS Code.

docs.title: 3. Basic use
docs.text:
catalog.save_polars("people", df)
catalog.load_polars("people")
catalog.load_polars("people", where="id > 1", columns=["name"])

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: D103, INP001, T201
"""Load a connection and use it from a catalog.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/connections_catalog.py``. It writes its
connections file, its catalog and its data under a temporary directory.
"""

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog
from smallcat.connections_config import ConnectionNotLoadedError

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="smallcat-conn-catalog-"))


def title(text: str) -> None:
    print(f"\n=== {text}")


# 1. The connection: defined once, in a file -----------------------------------
(workdir / "connections.yaml").write_text(
    f"""
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "lake").as_posix()}
""",
)
conns = Connections.from_yaml(workdir / "connections.yaml")
print(conns)

# 2. The catalog: each entry names the connection ------------------------------
(workdir / "catalog.yaml").write_text(
    """
entries:
  people:
    file_format: csv
    connection: lake
    location: people.csv
    load_options: {header: true}
    save_options: {header: true}
""",
)
catalog = Catalog.from_yaml(workdir / "catalog.yaml", connections=conns)

# 3. Basic use -----------------------------------------------------------------
title("save and load")
df = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["ada", "linus", "grace"]})
catalog.save_polars("people", df)
print("load           ", catalog.load_polars("people").rows())
print(
    "where + columns",
    catalog.load_polars("people", where="id > 1", columns=["name"]).rows(),
)

# 4. A name that was never loaded ----------------------------------------------
title("an entry that names a connection that is not loaded")
try:
    Catalog.from_dict(
        {
            "entries": {
                "sales": {
                    "file_format": "csv",
                    "connection": "warehouse",
                    "location": "sales.csv",
                },
            },
        },
        connections=conns,
    )
except ConnectionNotLoadedError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, "-", e)

docs.title: What it prints
docs.text:
Connections(lake:fs)

=== save and load
load            [(1, 'ada'), (2, 'linus'), (3, 'grace')]
where + columns [('linus',), ('grace',)]

An entry that names a connection that was not loaded fails when the catalog is loaded, before anything is read. The message lists the entry and the names that are available:

=== an entry that names a connection that is not loaded
ConnectionNotLoadedError - Connections not loaded: entry 'sales' uses 'warehouse' (available: lake)

Without connections=, a name is still resolved through Airflow the first time it is used. To load from Airflow instead of a file, see Connections.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Airflow: the same catalog in a DAG.
  • Querying a catalog, Writing with a catalog and the catalog reference.
  • The same connection used from a model: Connections with the ORM.

docs.title: Parquet on GCS: load and scan
docs.text:
On Google Cloud Storage the two ways of reading a Parquet file use different engines, and each one understands a different kind of credential:

Method Engine Credential it needs load_polars DuckDB HMAC keys (login and password) scan_polars Polars Service account (keyfile_dict, keyfile or key_path)

You do not need two connections. One connection can carry both, and each engine picks the one it understands.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
# connections.yaml
connections:
  gcs:
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    login: GOOG1E...                   # HMAC key id      -> load_polars
    password: <hmac-secret>            # HMAC secret      -> load_polars
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      key_path: /secrets/sa.json       # service account  -> scan_polars

Only one of keyfile_dict, keyfile and key_path may be set. login and password must come together. See Connect to Google Cloud Storage for every credential option, and how to load the connection.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text:
# catalog.yaml
entries:
  sales:
    file_format: parquet
    connection: gcs                    # the name defined above
    location: sales/2024/*.parquet

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import polars as pl
from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.catalog import Catalog

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")
catalog = Catalog.from_yaml("catalog.yaml", connections=conns)

# DuckDB reads and filters with SQL. Uses the HMAC keys.
eager = catalog.load_polars(
    "sales",
    where="country = 'ES' AND amount > 100",
    columns=["date", "amount"],
)

# Polars reads lazily. Uses the service account.
lazy = (
    catalog.scan_polars("sales")
    .filter((pl.col("country") == "ES") & (pl.col("amount") > 100))
    .select("date", "amount")
)
df = lazy.collect()   # only the needed columns and row groups are downloaded

Both return the same rows. scan_polars pushes the filter and the columns into the read, which is what saves bandwidth on a bucket; see Lazy scans.

docs.title: When a credential is missing
docs.text:
A missing credential does not fail silently at connection time. smallcat emits a UserWarning and the read goes on without credentials, so on a private bucket it then fails with a permissions error from GCS:

Connection has load_polars scan_polars HMAC keys and service account works works Only HMAC keys works UserWarning, reads anonymously Only a service account UserWarning, reads anonymously works

If you only ever use one of the two methods, one kind of credential is enough.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Unifying the authentication so that one credential serves both engines is tracked in issue #9.
  • The service account path of scan_polars is covered by unit tests that check the options handed to Polars, not by a test against a real bucket.
  • scan_polars on Parquet does not support the DuckDB-only load options binary_as_string and file_row_number; it raises a ValueError. Use load_polars for those.

docs.title: Connect to CSV files
docs.text:
A connection to a folder of files on the local filesystem. It says where the files are; what is in them and how they are read is up to whatever uses the connection. It needs nothing but smallcat-chonk, and the script writes its file under a temporary directory.

pip install smallcat-chonk
python connections_csv.py

docs.title: Define it
docs.text:
# connections.yaml
connections:
  local:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: /data         # or base_uri: file:///data

fs has no credentials. base_path is the folder every location is relative to: asking for people.csv through this connection means /data/people.csv. Without extra, locations are relative to the working directory.

Each connection has a name (local). Whatever uses it refers to it by that name, never by its content.

docs.title: Load it
docs.text:
from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

It is validated here, so a mistake fails at start-up and not on the first read.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: D103, INP001, T201
"""Define a connection to a folder of CSV files and load it.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/connections_csv.py``. It writes its
connections file under a temporary directory and touches nothing else.
"""

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.connections_config import ConnectionsValidationError

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="smallcat-csv-"))


def title(text: str) -> None:
    print(f"\n=== {text}")


# 1. Define it in a file -------------------------------------------------------
(workdir / "connections.yaml").write_text(
    f"""
connections:
  local:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "data").as_posix()}
""",
)

# 2. Load it: it is validated here ---------------------------------------------
conns = Connections.from_yaml(workdir / "connections.yaml")

title("what is loaded")
print("repr           ", conns)
print("names          ", conns.names())
print("'local' in     ", "local" in conns)

title("the definition, as a dataset receives it")
local = conns.get("local")
print("conn_type      ", local["conn_type"])  # type: ignore[index]
print("base_path      ", Path(local["extra"]["base_path"]).name)  # type: ignore[index]

# 3. A wrong definition fails when it is loaded --------------------------------
title("a typo is reported, not ignored")
try:
    Connections.from_dict(
        {"connections": {"local": {"conn_type": "fs", "extra": {"base_pth": "/data"}}}},
    )
except ConnectionsValidationError as e:
    print(e)

docs.title: What it prints
docs.text:
=== what is loaded
repr            Connections(local:fs)
names           ['local']
'local' in      True

=== the definition, as a dataset receives it
conn_type       fs
base_path       data

repr shows names and types only, so a credential can never end up in a log. get hands out the definition as a plain dictionary, ready for a dataset.

A wrong definition is refused when it is loaded. Unknown keys are rejected, so a typo is reported instead of silently ignored:

=== a typo is reported, not ignored
Invalid connections:
  - local.extra.base_pth: Extra inputs are not permitted

docs.title: Next
docs.text: The same file can hold connections to a bucket: Google Cloud Storage and Amazon S3. See Connections for the loaders and the errors.

docs.title: Connect to Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
A connection to a bucket. It says which bucket and prefix to use and how to authenticate.

# connections.yaml
connections:
  gcs_hmac:
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    login: GOOG1E...               # HMAC key id
    password: <hmac-secret>        # HMAC secret
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      prefix: raw                  # or base_uri: gs://my-bucket/raw

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

Asking for sales/2024.csv through this connection means gs://my-bucket/raw/sales/2024.csv. google is accepted as an alias of google_cloud_platform.

docs.title: Which credential
docs.text:
It depends on the engine that reads the data, not only on the format:

Data Read with Credential CSV, Excel or Parquet, loaded eagerly DuckDB HMAC keys: login and password Parquet, scanned lazily Polars Service account A Delta table delta-rs Service account

A service account goes in extra, with one of key_path (a file), keyfile (the JSON as a string) or keyfile_dict (the JSON as a mapping):

connections:
  gcs_sa:
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      key_path: /secrets/service-account.json

One connection can carry both kinds, and each engine picks the one it understands.

docs.title: Validated when loaded
docs.text:
Nothing is read when the connections are loaded, but a wrong definition fails right there. The script below loads these definitions with placeholder keys, so it needs no bucket and no network:

loaded          Connections(gcs_hmac:google_cloud_platform, gcs_sa:google_cloud_platform)

=== secrets never show up
password        False
get() is plain  example-hmac-secret

=== what is refused, when the connections are loaded
key id without secret  Value error, GCS HMAC keys need both `login` (key id) and `password` (secret).
two service accounts   Value error, Provide only one service account source, found `keyfile`, `key_path`.
  • The secret is not in repr(conns), so it cannot end up in a log.
  • A missing credential is not an error: smallcat warns and the read goes on without credentials, so on a private bucket it fails with a permissions error from GCS.

Note

The secrets are plain text in the YAML file. Keep the file out of version control, or load the connections from Airflow (Connections.from_airflow).

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: D103, INP001, T201
"""Define connections to Google Cloud Storage, without a network.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/connections_gcs.py``. It only loads and
validates the definitions, so it needs no bucket and no credentials: the keys
below are placeholders. Nothing is read or written.
"""

import yaml

from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.connections_config import ConnectionsValidationError

CONNECTIONS = yaml.safe_load(
    """
connections:
  gcs_hmac:                       # HMAC keys: DuckDB
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    login: GOOG1EXAMPLEKEYID      # HMAC key id
    password: example-hmac-secret # HMAC secret
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      prefix: raw
  gcs_sa:                         # service account: Polars and delta-rs
    conn_type: google_cloud_platform
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      key_path: /secrets/service-account.json
""",
)

conns = Connections.from_dict(CONNECTIONS)
print("loaded         ", conns)

print("\n=== secrets never show up")
print("password       ", "example-hmac-secret" in repr(conns))
print("get() is plain ", conns.get("gcs_hmac")["password"])  # type: ignore[index]

print("\n=== what is refused, when the connections are loaded")
BAD = {
    "key id without secret": {
        "conn_type": "google_cloud_platform",
        "login": "GOOG1EXAMPLEKEYID",
        "extra": {"bucket": "b"},
    },
    "two service accounts": {
        "conn_type": "google_cloud_platform",
        "extra": {"bucket": "b", "key_path": "/a.json", "keyfile": "{}"},
    },
}
for label, definition in BAD.items():
    try:
        Connections.from_dict({"connections": {"bad": definition}})
    except ConnectionsValidationError as e:
        reason = str(e).splitlines()[1].strip()
        print(f"{label:22}", reason.removeprefix("- bad: "))

Run it with python connections_gcs.py.

docs.title: Connect to Amazon S3
docs.text:
A connection to a bucket. It says which bucket, prefix and region to use and how to authenticate.

# connections.yaml
connections:
  s3_chain:
    conn_type: aws
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      prefix: raw                  # or base_uri: s3://my-bucket/raw
      region_name: eu-west-1

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

Asking for sales/2024.csv through this connection means s3://my-bucket/raw/sales/2024.csv. s3 is accepted as an alias of aws.

docs.title: Which credential
docs.text:
There are two ways, and they cannot be mixed.

IAM roles and the AWS credential chain (recommended). Leave login and password out, as above. The credentials are found the way the AWS SDK finds them: environment variables, web identity (EKS), ECS task roles, EC2 instance profiles, SSO and the shared AWS files. To assume a role, define a profile with role_arn and source_profile in ~/.aws/config and name it:

connections:
  s3_profile:
    conn_type: aws
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      profile_name: dev

Static keys. login is the access key id and password the secret access key, plus aws_session_token for temporary keys:

connections:
  s3_keys:
    conn_type: aws
    login: AKIA...
    password: <secret-access-key>
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      region_name: eu-west-1

An S3-compatible store, such as MinIO, takes an endpoint_url:

connections:
  s3_minio:
    conn_type: aws
    login: minio
    password: <secret>
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      endpoint_url: http://minio:9000

docs.title: Validated when loaded
docs.text:
A wrong combination fails when the connections are loaded, with nothing read:

  • login and password must come together.
  • Static keys cannot be combined with profile_name.
  • aws_session_token needs static keys.

The script below loads these definitions with placeholder keys, so it needs no bucket and no network:

loaded          Connections(s3_chain:aws, s3_profile:aws, s3_keys:aws, s3_minio:aws)

=== secrets never show up
password        False
get() is plain  example-secret-access-key

=== what is refused, when the connections are loaded
key id without secret  Value error, AWS static keys need both `login` (access key id) and `password`.
keys and a profile     Value error, `profile_name` cannot be combined with static keys (login/password): remove the keys to use the AWS credential chain.
session token only     Value error, `aws_session_token` needs static keys (login/password).

The secret is not in repr(conns), so it cannot end up in a log.

Note

The secrets are plain text in the YAML file. Prefer the credential chain, or load the connections from Airflow (Connections.from_airflow).

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: D103, INP001, T201
"""Define connections to Amazon S3, without a network.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/connections_s3.py``. It only loads and
validates the definitions, so it needs no bucket and no credentials: the keys
below are placeholders. Nothing is read or written.
"""

import yaml

from smallcat import Connections
from smallcat.connections_config import ConnectionsValidationError

CONNECTIONS = yaml.safe_load(
    """
connections:
  s3_chain:                       # IAM role / AWS credential chain
    conn_type: aws
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      prefix: raw
      region_name: eu-west-1
  s3_profile:                     # a profile of ~/.aws/config
    conn_type: aws
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      profile_name: dev
  s3_keys:                        # static keys
    conn_type: aws
    login: AKIAEXAMPLEKEYID
    password: example-secret-access-key
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      region_name: eu-west-1
  s3_minio:                       # an S3-compatible store
    conn_type: aws
    login: minio
    password: minio-secret
    extra:
      bucket: my-bucket
      endpoint_url: http://minio:9000
""",
)

conns = Connections.from_dict(CONNECTIONS)
print("loaded         ", conns)

print("\n=== secrets never show up")
print("password       ", "example-secret-access-key" in repr(conns))
print("get() is plain ", conns.get("s3_keys")["password"])  # type: ignore[index]

print("\n=== what is refused, when the connections are loaded")
BAD = {
    "key id without secret": {
        "conn_type": "aws",
        "login": "AKIAEXAMPLEKEYID",
        "extra": {"bucket": "b"},
    },
    "keys and a profile": {
        "conn_type": "aws",
        "login": "AKIAEXAMPLEKEYID",
        "password": "example-secret-access-key",
        "extra": {"bucket": "b", "profile_name": "dev"},
    },
    "session token only": {
        "conn_type": "aws",
        "extra": {"bucket": "b", "aws_session_token": "token"},
    },
}
for label, definition in BAD.items():
    try:
        Connections.from_dict({"connections": {"bad": definition}})
    except ConnectionsValidationError as e:
        reason = str(e).splitlines()[1].strip()
        print(f"{label:22}", reason.removeprefix("- bad: "))

Run it with python connections_s3.py. See Connections for the loaders and the errors.

docs.title: Connections with the ORM
docs.text:
How a connection reaches a model: define it once in a file, load it into the registry, and say which connection the model uses when you register it. The model itself never names a connection. It needs nothing but smallcat-chonk; the script writes its files under a temporary directory.

pip install smallcat-chonk
python connections_orm.py

docs.title: 1. Define and load the connections
docs.text:
# connections.yaml
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: /data
  archive:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: /archive

from smallcat import Connections

conns = Connections.from_yaml("connections.yaml")

For a bucket, only this definition changes: see Google Cloud Storage and Amazon S3.

docs.title: 2. Define the model
docs.text:
from smallcat import Model, ModelFileFormat

class Person(Model):
    id: int
    name: str

    class Meta:
        location = "people.csv"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.CSV

docs.title: 3. Load the connections into the registry and register the model
docs.text:
from smallcat import registry

registry.load_connections(conns)
registry.register(Person, connection="lake")

register is where the connection is chosen, outside the model, so the same model can run against different storage in each environment.

docs.title: 4. Basic use
docs.text:
import polars as pl
from smallcat import ModelWriteMode

Person.objects.save(df, mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE)
Person.objects.all()
Person.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 1).all()

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: D101, D103, D106, INP001, T201
"""Load a connection and use it from a model.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/connections_orm.py``. It writes its
connections file and its data under a temporary directory.
"""

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from smallcat import Connections, Model, ModelFileFormat, ModelWriteMode, registry

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="smallcat-conn-orm-"))


def title(text: str) -> None:
    print(f"\n=== {text}")


# 1. The connections: defined once, in a file ----------------------------------
(workdir / "connections.yaml").write_text(
    f"""
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "lake").as_posix()}
  archive:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "archive").as_posix()}
""",
)
conns = Connections.from_yaml(workdir / "connections.yaml")
print(conns)


# 2. The model never names a connection ----------------------------------------
class Person(Model):
    id: int
    name: str

    class Meta:
        location = "people.csv"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.CSV


# 3. The registry loads the connections and says which one the model uses ------
registry.load_connections(conns)
registry.register(Person, connection="lake")

# 4. Basic use -----------------------------------------------------------------
title("save and read")
df = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["ada", "linus", "grace"]})
Person.objects.save(df, mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE)
print("all            ", Person.objects.all().rows())
print("filter         ", Person.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 1).all().rows())

# 5. Other storage, same model: only the registration changes ------------------
title("the same model on other storage")
registry.register(Person, connection="archive", replace=True)
Person.objects.save(pl.DataFrame({"id": [9], "name": ["alan"]}), mode="overwrite")
print("archive        ", Person.objects.all().rows())
registry.register(Person, connection="lake", replace=True)
print("lake, untouched", Person.objects.all().rows())

# 6. A name that was never loaded ----------------------------------------------
title("a connection that is not loaded")
try:
    registry.register(Person, connection="warehouse", replace=True)
except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
    print(type(e).__name__, "-", e)

docs.title: Models on the local filesystem
docs.text:
A runnable walk-through of models: connections from a file, a Parquet model, a Delta model, a read-only model, writing, and what the guard rails refuse. For reading and filtering, see Querying. It needs nothing but smallcat-chonk; it writes its connections file and its data under a temporary directory.

pip install smallcat-chonk
python models_local.py

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: CPY001, D101, D106, DTZ001, INP001, RUF012, T201
"""Defining, registering and writing models on the local filesystem.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/models_local.py``. It needs nothing but
smallcat-chonk: it writes its connections file and its data under a temporary
directory.
"""

import tempfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from smallcat import (
    Connections,
    Model,
    ModelFileFormat,
    ModelRegistry,
    ModelWriteMode,
    registry,
    use_registry,
)
from smallcat.models import (
    ModelSchemaValidationError,
    ModelUnsupportedWriteModeError,
    ModelWriteNotAllowedError,
)

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="smallcat-models-"))

# 1. Connections live in a file (or in Airflow), never in the code. ----------
(workdir / "connections.yaml").write_text(
    f"""
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "lake").as_posix()}
""",
)


# 2. Models say what the data is. They know nothing about connections. --------
class Customer(Model):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str | None = None
    created_at: datetime

    class Meta:
        location = "silver/customers.parquet"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.PARQUET
        allowed_write_modes = [ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE]  # a file is replaced whole


class Event(Model):
    id: int
    kind: str

    class Meta:
        location = "silver/events"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.DELTA_TABLE  # Delta can also append and merge
        merge_keys = ["id"]  # what identifies a row for mode="merge"


class Report(Model):
    id: int
    total: float

    class Meta:
        location = "gold/report.parquet"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.PARQUET
        allowed_write_modes = []  # read-only


# 3. The environment binds models to connections. -----------------------------
registry.load_connections(Connections.from_yaml(workdir / "connections.yaml"))
for model in (Customer, Event, Report):
    registry.register(model, connection="lake")

# 4. Write. `mode` is always explicit. ----------------------------------------
Customer.objects.save(
    [
        Customer(
            id=1,
            name="Ada",
            email="ada@example.com",
            created_at=datetime(2024, 1, 5),
        ),
        Customer(id=2, name="Linus", created_at=datetime(2024, 3, 9)),
        Customer(
            id=3,
            name="Grace",
            email="grace@example.com",
            created_at=datetime(2025, 2, 1),
        ),
    ],
    mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE,
)
# A NaN (what pandas gives for an empty cell) in a `T | None` field is stored as
# None, so no validator of your own is needed.
print(
    "-- NaN in a nullable field:",
    Customer(
        id=4,
        name="Alan",
        email=float("nan"),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        created_at=datetime(2025, 5, 1),
    ).email,
)
Event.objects.save(
    pl.DataFrame({"id": [1], "kind": ["signup"]}),
    mode=ModelWriteMode.APPEND,
)
Event.objects.save(
    pl.DataFrame({"id": [2], "kind": ["login"]}),
    mode=ModelWriteMode.APPEND,
)
# Merge: id 2 exists, so it is updated; id 3 is new, so it is inserted.
Event.objects.save(
    pl.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "kind": ["logout", "purchase"]}),
    mode=ModelWriteMode.MERGE,
)

# 5. Read it back. Filtering and the other ways to read are in "Querying". -------
print("-- all customers")
print(Customer.objects.all().sort("id"))

print("-- events (appended twice, then merged)")
print(Event.objects.all().sort("id"))

# 6. What the guard rails refuse. -------------------------------------------------
print("-- refusals")
for label, action in {
    "wrong types": lambda: Customer.objects.save(
        pl.DataFrame(
            {
                "id": ["1"],
                "name": ["x"],
                "email": [None],
                "created_at": [datetime(2024, 1, 1)],
            },
        ),
        mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE,
    ),
    "append, which the model does not allow": lambda: Customer.objects.save(
        [],
        mode=ModelWriteMode.APPEND,
    ),
    "write a read-only model": lambda: Report.objects.save(
        pl.DataFrame({"id": [1], "total": [1.0]}),
        mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE,
    ),
}.items():
    try:
        action()
    except (
        ModelSchemaValidationError,
        ModelUnsupportedWriteModeError,
        ModelWriteNotAllowedError,
    ) as error:
        print(f"[{label}] {type(error).__name__}: {error}")

# 7. Tests (or another environment) use a registry of their own. ------------------
test_registry = ModelRegistry()
test_registry.load_connections(
    Connections.from_dict(
        {
            "connections": {
                "lake": {
                    "conn_type": "fs",
                    "extra": {"base_path": str(workdir / "test-lake")},
                },
            },
        },
    ),
)
test_registry.register(Customer, connection="lake")
with use_registry(test_registry):
    Customer.objects.save([], mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE)
    print(
        "-- inside use_registry the data is separate:",
        Customer.objects.all().height,
        "rows",
    )
print("-- outside it is untouched:", Customer.objects.all().height, "rows")

The Parquet model was saved whole, and read back:

-- all customers
shape: (3, 4)
┌─────┬───────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ name  ┆ email             ┆ created_at          │

└─────┴───────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────────┘

The Delta model was appended to twice and then merged by id: row 2 already existed, so it was updated (login became logout), and row 3 was new, so it was inserted. Nothing was deleted:

-- events (appended twice, then merged)
shape: (3, 2)
┌─────┬──────────┐
│ id  ┆ kind     │
│ --- ┆ ---      │

│ 2   ┆ logout   │
│ 3   ┆ purchase │
└─────┴──────────┘

And what is refused, each one before anything is written:

-- refusals
[wrong types] ModelSchemaValidationError: Customer does not match its schema:
  - id: expected Int64, got String
[append, which the model does not allow] ModelWriteNotAllowedError: Customer does not allow 'append' (allowed: ['overwrite'])
[write a read-only model] ModelWriteNotAllowedError: Report is read-only: it allows no write mode

-- outside it is untouched: 3 rows

docs.title: With Airflow
docs.text:
Only the connections change. Replace the YAML loader and nothing else:

registry.load_connections(Connections.from_airflow(["lake"]))
registry.register(Customer, connection="lake")

The ids are resolved and validated at that line, so a connection that is missing in Airflow fails at start-up and not on the first read.

docs.title: Querying a model on the local filesystem
docs.text:
A runnable walk-through of reading a model: all(), filter() with Polars expressions, where() with SQL and with lookups, select(), lazy() and as_models(). The connection, the model and the registration are the ones in Models and Connections with the ORM; here they are the first lines of the script and the rest is the query. It needs nothing but smallcat-chonk; it writes its connections file and its data under a temporary directory.

pip install smallcat-chonk
python models_querying.py

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ruff: noqa: CPY001, D101, D106, DTZ001, INP001, RUF012, T201
"""Querying a model on the local filesystem.

Run it with ``python docs/examples/models_querying.py``. It needs nothing but
smallcat-chonk: it writes its connections file and its data under a temporary
directory.
"""

import tempfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from smallcat import (
    Connections,
    Model,
    ModelFileFormat,
    ModelWriteMode,
    registry,
)
from smallcat.models import ModelQueryError

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="smallcat-querying-"))

# 1. The connection and the model (see "Models" for the details). ------------------
(workdir / "connections.yaml").write_text(
    f"""
connections:
  lake:
    conn_type: fs
    extra:
      base_path: {(workdir / "lake").as_posix()}
""",
)


class Customer(Model):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str | None = None
    created_at: datetime

    class Meta:
        location = "silver/customers.parquet"
        file_format = ModelFileFormat.PARQUET


registry.load_connections(Connections.from_yaml(workdir / "connections.yaml"))
registry.register(Customer, connection="lake")

Customer.objects.save(
    [
        Customer(
            id=1,
            name="Ada",
            email="ada@example.com",
            created_at=datetime(2024, 1, 5),
        ),
        Customer(id=2, name="Linus", created_at=datetime(2024, 3, 9)),
        Customer(
            id=3,
            name="Grace",
            email="grace@example.com",
            created_at=datetime(2025, 2, 1),
        ),
    ],
    mode=ModelWriteMode.OVERWRITE,
)

# 2. Query it. -----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("-- all customers")
print(Customer.objects.all().sort("id"))

print("-- filter with Polars expressions, project two fields")
print(
    Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("created_at") >= datetime(2024, 3, 1))
    .select("id", "name")
    .all()
    .sort("id"),
)

print("-- the same, lazily: the filter is pushed down into the Parquet scan")
print(Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 1).select("name").lazy().explain())

print("-- or with SQL")
print(Customer.objects.where("email IS NOT NULL").select("name").all().sort("name"))

print("-- or with lookups")
print(Customer.objects.where(id__gte=2).select("name").all().sort("name"))

print("-- as model instances")
print(Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") == 1).all(as_models=True))
print(Customer.objects.all(as_models=True))  # also on the manager

# 3. A query is a value, and contradictory ones are refused where they are written. -
print("-- a query is not run until you ask")
recent = Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 1)
print("rows :", recent.all().height)
print("again:", recent.filter(pl.col("id") > 2).all().height, "(recent is unchanged)")

print("-- refusals")
try:
    Customer.objects.filter(pl.col("id") > 1).where("id < 3")
except ModelQueryError as error:
    print(f"[filter + where] {type(error).__name__}: {error}")

docs.title: What it prints
docs.text:
Every row, and the same data filtered with Polars expressions, keeping two fields:

-- all customers
shape: (3, 4)
┌─────┬───────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ name  ┆ email             ┆ created_at          │
│ --- ┆ ---   ┆ ---               ┆ ---                 │
│ i64 ┆ str   ┆ str               ┆ datetime[μs]        │
╞═════╪═══════╪═══════════════════╪═════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ Ada   ┆ ada@example.com   ┆ 2024-01-05 00:00:00 │
│ 2   ┆ Linus ┆ null              ┆ 2024-03-09 00:00:00 │
│ 3   ┆ Grace ┆ grace@example.com ┆ 2025-02-01 00:00:00 │
└─────┴───────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
-- filter with Polars expressions, project two fields
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬───────┐
│ id  ┆ name  │
│ --- ┆ ---   │
│ i64 ┆ str   │
╞═════╪═══════╡
│ 2   ┆ Linus │
│ 3   ┆ Grace │
└─────┴───────┘

The same query lazily. The filter shows up as SELECTION and the columns as PROJECT 2/4, inside the Parquet scan: they are pushed down to the file, so only what is needed is read:

-- the same, lazily: the filter is pushed down into the Parquet scan
simple π 1/1 ["name"]
  Parquet SCAN [file:///.../lake/silver/customers.parquet]
  PROJECT 2/4 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: col("id") > 1
  ESTIMATED ROWS: 3

The same kind of filter written as SQL, as lookups, and read back as model instances:

-- or with SQL
shape: (2, 1)
┌───────┐
│ name  │
│ ---   │
│ str   │
╞═══════╡
│ Ada   │
│ Grace │
└───────┘
-- or with lookups
shape: (2, 1)
┌───────┐
│ name  │
│ ---   │
│ str   │
╞═══════╡
│ Grace │
│ Linus │
└───────┘
-- as model instances
[Customer(id=1, name='Ada', email='ada@example.com', created_at=datetime.datetime(2024, 1, 5, 0, 0))]

A query is a value: filtering it again returns a new query and leaves the first one as it was. Nothing is read until all(), lazy() or as_models(). And filter() with where() cannot be combined: it is refused where it is written, not when it runs:

-- a query is not run until you ask
rows : 2
again: 1 (recent is unchanged)
-- refusals
[filter + where] ModelQueryError: filter() takes Polars expressions and where() takes an SQL predicate: a query can use only one of them
